correctness.rationale: The construction was rebuilt from definitions. Cardinality is bounded by \(\kappa\) because each initial stage has at most \(2^{|\alpha|}\le\kappa\) hereditary types. Heredity is preserved even when a subset changes the maximal vertex because labels along a chain are exact restrictions. The canonical map for any target family is an exact restriction embedding, and the coordinate projection is contractive. Composing with the focal source's contractive projection proves the \(1\)-complemented isometric monotone-basis consequence.

originality.rationale: The focal paper proves an intended complemented-universality theorem via hereditary closure of a universal hypergraph, but its explicit Proposition 7.5 coding does not survive that closure: every finite subset of the canonical coding range enters the closure. The new claim replaces that step by a coherent-initial-type hereditary family and obtains exact restriction, hence norm-one isometric coordinate universality. The 2024 predecessor gives the exact hereditary-universal construction only in the countable Fraïssé setting. Targeted published-finding corpus searches found no implication-equivalent cardinal-\(\kappa\) exact hereditary construction or the associated \(1\)-complemented isometric Banach consequence.
residual_risks: A general model-theoretic universal-structure theorem may subsume the set-system construction abstractly under additional or equivalent cardinal arithmetic; no inspected source gave the exact statement used here.
The full implication from existence of an arbitrary universal hypergraph to existence of a universal combinatorial Banach space is not settled by this finding.
The norm-one isometric consequence is asserted only for monotone unconditional bases; no quantitative claim is made for arbitrary unconditional bases.

value.rationale: The issue is structural rather than cosmetic: hereditary closure can destroy the encoded finite-set relations needed for coordinate copies. The coherent-type construction supplies the exact missing property and upgrades the positive consequence to norm-one isometric universality for monotone unconditional bases under the same explicit cardinal bound. This directly addresses the mechanism of a recent universal-space construction and generalizes the exact countable hereditary-universal picture.
